item.title: In 1998, 31 Przewalski’s horses entered Chernobyl and reached 137 by 2018
item.description: After the Chernobyl disaster, an abandoned radioactive landscape became an unlikely refuge for Przewalski’s horses, a species once lost from the wild. Introduced in 1998–99, the population suffered transport deaths and poaching but continued breeding. By 2018, 137 horses were documented in Ukraine, with others established across the Belarusian border.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indian-origin UK nurse wins $250,000 Global Nursing Award for boosting organ donation among South Asians
item.description: In a remarkable achievement, Indian-origin nurse Agimol Pradeep has clinched the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026, celebrated for her impactful advocacy in organ and stem-cell donation. The $250,000 award will see half allocated to Upahaar's efforts in expanding organ donation initiatives. This recognition not only emphasizes the vital contributions of nurses to healthcare but also aligns with Kerala's efforts to bolster its nursing workforce amid persistent global shortages.

item.title: Streamer Ejected From Scientology Church: Peters screams for help; then urges crowd to seek Jesus
item.description: Braden “Clavicular” Peters was removed from the Church of Scientology in Los Angeles during his Hollywood livestream after repeatedly calling for help and claiming people were trying to kill him. Outside, he continued speaking to people near the building and repeatedly told them they needed God and Jesus Christ. A clip of the confrontation was later shared on X.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Owens Presses For Surveillance Details: Conservative demands suspect info; Turning Point reviews footage
item.description: Candace Owens has questioned Turning Point Action over the vandalism of Charlie Kirk’s memorial statue at the organisation’s Arizona headquarters. She urged the group to share more details from its surveillance cameras, including descriptions of the suspects or their vehicle, so the public could help identify those responsible. Turning Point condemned the incident and said it was working with law enforcement while planning to restore the damaged statue.

item.title: Kai Cenat And Gigi Alayah Reunion Rumors? North West reacts on TikTok; Fashion Week sightings revive questions
item.description: Kai Cenat and Gabrielle “Gigi” Alayah have sparked fresh reunion rumors after being spotted together during New York Fashion Week. Cenat was seen blowing kisses to Alayah after his Vivet runway show, with her appearing to return the gesture. North West then added to the speculation by commenting on Alayah’s TikTok, “can’t believe that u n kai are back together.” Neither has confirmed that they are dating again.

item.title: Texas bought a 1,700-acre Hill Country ranch for a new state park; planners want it ruggeda
item.description: Texas park authorities are setting in motion the development of Bear Creek State Park on a newly acquired ranch. This park promises to deliver a wild and authentic outdoor adventure, featuring backcountry trails and restricted vehicle access to help protect delicate ecosystems. The aim is to foster a serene recreational environment while also preserving the pristine night skies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1990, mining stopped at a 55-metre-deep Swedish limestone quarry; a year later...
item.description: Once a bustling mining site, Dalhalla is now a stunning open-air concert venue nestled in an abandoned Swedish quarry. Renowned for its outstanding natural acoustics discovered in 1991, this breathtaking locale invites performers and audiences alike to bask in the unique ambiance created by limestone walls shaped by an ancient meteorite impact. Annually, it enchants over 100,000 visitors, adding to the charm of the Dalarna region.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A US grandfather planned a $150,000 treehouse for his grandkids; it grew into a $325,000 castle
item.description: What started as a simple backyard play area vision transformed into a stunning treehouse sanctuary. Priced at $325,000, this remarkable creation boasts a pirate ship and an exciting zipline. Meticulously designed by professional engineers, the treehouse prioritizes safety and the health of the trees. Its multi-tiered layout offers cozy lofts perfect for family bonding and unforgettable gatherings, making it an enduring family attraction filled with wonder and creativity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1835, Free Frank McWorter, a formerly enslaved man, paid $100 for 80 Illinois acres
item.description: The Hampshire House in Manhattan has seen its unfinished penthouse sell for $6.765 million, a staggering reduction of 83% from its original listing of $40 million. This raw attic space demanded substantial work to become livable. After years of challenges and strategic efforts, it was sold through an online auction, highlighting the complexities of luxury real estate dealings in New York City.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Los Angeles home used by Apple, Google and Walmart for filming, listed for $3.245 million
item.description: A Woodland Hills home in Los Angeles that has hosted 173 productions since 2021 is now on the market for $3.245 million. The 4,675-sq-ft property has earned more than $1.5 million from filming. The sale also includes the established Rum Punch House filming business, industry contacts, website and production-related infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: At 84, 'Nan Barb' drives 2,000km monthly to deliver donated clothes; community raises money for truck
item.description: At the age of 84, Nan Barb is a remarkable woman who travels over two thousand kilometers each month. She dedicates her time to delivering donated clothing from her op shop to remote communities throughout Western Australia. Her efforts bridge the gap for those in isolated areas who require essential goods, and the community is actively fundraising to secure a larger truck to enhance her vital mission.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Massachusetts dairy turned cow manure and food waste into energy; it now saves thousands on heat, fertiliser and bedding
item.description: Jordan Dairy Farms in Rutland, Massachusetts, embraces cutting-edge anaerobic digestion technology to revolutionize waste management. By transforming cow manure and food scraps into energy and fertilizer, the farm not only boosts its sustainability but also slashes operational costs. This innovative approach not only supports the farm’s productivity but also significantly mitigates its environmental footprint, showcasing a model for responsible agriculture.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
